record_type_quote: In a replication of this experiment conducted with 128 volunteers, we did not observe evidence for a mortality salience effect.

targets.authors: Goldenberg JL, Pyszczynski T, Greenberg J, Solomon S, Kluck B, Cornwell R
targets.title: I am not an animal: mortality salience, disgust, and the denial of human creatureliness
targets.evidence_quote: The present study replicated the procedure followed in Study 2 by Goldenberg et al. [9].
targets.outcome_quote: Overall, the pattern of results reported in the previous section are inconsistent with the original results of Goldenberg et al. [9].
targets.outcome_reasoning: Explicit overall verdict of inconsistency with the original.

targets.authors: Burke BL, Martens A, Faucher EH
targets.title: Two decades of terror management theory: a meta-analysis of mortality salience research
targets.evidence_quote: Our own inspection of the data reported by Burke et al. [3] converges to the conclusion that the robustness of these effect sizes may have been overestimated.
targets.outcome_computational_quote: Instead of analysing raw correlation coefficients, which are constrained to adopt values from −1 to +1 and do not follow a normal distribution, we converted all effect sizes to Fisher's z scores.
targets.outcome_robustness_quote: Consistent with the former interpretation, our own reanalysis of Burke et al. ([3]; see also [11]) provides compelling evidence that the effect sizes of previous research on mortality salience may have been overestimated.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Same meta-analytic data reanalysed using bias-sensitive alternatives; bias-corrected effect 37% smaller and original absence-of-bias conclusion challenged. Original-number reproduction was outside these alternative analyses.

reasoning: New-sample replication of Goldenberg Study 2 plus an independently coded original-data reanalysis of Burke et al.; reproduction axes used for the latter. Other mortality-salience studies are background, not retested targets.
